steps.say: We use words to say how likely something is to happen.
Certain means it will happen. Impossible means it can never happen.
steps.show: The sun will set this evening: certain

steps.say: Likely means it will probably happen. Unlikely means it probably will not.
This bag has 7 apples and 1 pear. Taking an apple is likely, and taking the pear is unlikely.

figure.alt: A bag with 7 apples and 1 pear.

check.prompt: A bag has 6 bananas. Hana takes one without looking. How likely is it to be a banana?

options.why: Unlikely means it probably will not happen.
Likely means it will probably happen. Here it will happen for sure.
Impossible means it can never happen.

hints: Look at every fruit in the bag.
Is there any fruit that is not a banana?
Think about what else could be taken.
check.explanation: Every fruit in the bag is a banana, so taking a banana is certain.

check.prompt: How likely is this? A normal dice numbered 1 to 6 shows a 7.

options.why: Unlikely means it could happen. A normal dice has no 7.
Certain means it will happen for sure. A normal dice has no 7.
Likely means it will probably happen. A normal dice has no 7.

hints: Think about the numbers on a normal dice.
Something that can never happen has its own word.
check.explanation: A normal dice only has the numbers 1 to 6, so rolling a 7 is impossible.
